claims.text: Fine-tuning compositional disorder governs the strong low-field magnetocaloric response of rare-earth-free high-entropy alloys.
An optimized level of compositional disorder optimizes local magnetic exchange interactions.
Compositional disorder can reduce magnetic anisotropy.
Reduced magnetic anisotropy enables a more uniform magnetization process.
Reduced magnetic anisotropy enables a more reversible magnetization process.
A more uniform and reversible magnetization process enhances the magnetocaloric effect.
Optimized compositional disorder minimizes magnetic hysteresis losses.
Optimized compositional disorder enhances heat exchange.
Optimized compositional disorder preserves mechanical stability.
Relative constituent-element concentrations can be varied while retaining a single-phase solid-solution structure.
Compared with the baseline, an optimized alloy will have a higher isothermal magnetic entropy change at applied fields below approximately 1 T.
Compared with the baseline, an optimized alloy will have a higher adiabatic temperature change at applied fields below approximately 1 T.
Compared with the baseline, an optimized alloy will exhibit reduced magnetic hysteresis.
Compared with the baseline, an optimized alloy will show no significant degradation in mechanical stability.
The proposed relationship should hold near the Curie temperature for single-phase solid-solution HEAs with moderate compositional disorder.
The proposed relationship may not apply to multiphase alloys or to alloys with extreme disorder that causes phase separation.
